findings.summary: CODEX-01-C adds local-only founder authentication: synthetic identities, password and authenticator-code (TOTP) login, and server-side sessions. It stays in the card's file scope and uses migration 003 without editing 001 or 002. All three card criteria are met in code and covered by a passing real PostgreSQL plus HTTP test: unauthenticated callers get 401 and family callers get 403; expiry, logout, demotion and disabling are checked against the database on every request; and secrets are absent from logs, console/stderr, responses and session rows, with every response set to no-store. All five extra checks the app review must confirm have actual tests: the cleared logout cookie, identical unknown-user and wrong-password replies, the lockout lifting after its window, refusal of bad Host, content type, oversized body and duplicate cookies, and console/stderr secret capture. The controller's npm test, build and card checker all exited 0. I could not read check_application_card.py or founder_auth_probe.mjs myself (permission denied), so for those I am relying on the controller's reported output. Remaining issues are minor and do not block the acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Login issues a new session but does not revoke the presented one
findings.problem: POST /login always issues a fresh server-generated token, so session fixation is not possible. But a valid loop_session cookie sent with the login request is never revoked, and the test shows the earlier founderCookie stays valid after re-login. The card says login 'rotates any client-proposed session'. The strictest reading means the replaced session should be invalidated, which would leave fewer live sessions.
findings.fix_check: On successful login, revoke the session for the presented cookie token (if any) in the same transaction. Add a test that the previous cookie returns 401 on GET /founder after re-login.

findings.title: 4KB streaming body limit is untested; report says 'chunked'
findings.problem: req.end(payload) on a fresh Node request sets Content-Length, so the 4097-byte test only hits the Content-Length check. The streaming size check (size > 4096 while reading) never runs. REPORT.md describes this as a '4097-byte chunked body', which overstates the evidence. The card explicitly requires the 4KB-body refusal.
findings.fix_check: Add a test that sends more than 4096 bytes with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and no Content-Length (e.g. several req.write calls) and gets 413. Correct the REPORT.md wording.

findings.title: Result report omits specific downstream task IDs
findings.problem: The card says completion must record 'downstream IDs from the index'. The report only lists module categories (intake, review, publication and so on) and WM-08/WM-10, with no specific task IDs. Its check section still says NOT YET RUN everywhere and does not point to the controller results now attached.
findings.fix_check: REPORT.md lists the downstream task IDs from INDEX.md and references the controller's npm test, build and checker results by revision.

findings.title: One global throttle lets any account lock out the founder
findings.problem: The single global throttle avoids leaking which accounts exist, and this is documented. The side effect is that failed attempts on any username, including a family account, block the founder from logging in until the window ends. This is acceptable for a disposable local issuer. Production rate-limit policy remains gated and should not inherit this design without a decision.
findings.fix_check: The report or code comment states this cross-account lockout trade-off as provisional local-only behaviour.

findings.title: Strict cookie parsing rejects requests with other 127.0.0.1 cookies
findings.problem: Browsers send 127.0.0.1 cookies to every port. Any cookie that fails the strict parser, or a duplicate name set by another local dev server, gets a 401 on every route, including GET /login. This is safe (it fails closed) but could confuse a developer.
findings.fix_check: Optional: only apply strict parsing and duplicate rejection to loop_session, or document the behaviour.
